red_paragraphs.red_text: Frames in which the pocket-lining Cα atoms were no longer a compact cluster, defined as a radius of gyration above 10 Å, were excluded. The apo cavity was not re-solvated with bulk water before measurement, which biases apo volumes low, so bound–unliganded volume differences are geometric upper bounds rather than estimates of a free-energy cost.

red_paragraphs.paragraph: Per-residue Cα root-mean-square fluctuation (RMSF) was computed after superposing every fr
red_paragraphs.red_text: Per-residue Cα root-mean-square fluctuation (RMSF) was computed after superposing every frame on the Cα atoms of the sixteen NNIBP-lining residues, so that the reported fluctuation is motion about each residue's own mean position with rigid-body translation and rotation of the pocket removed, and was then averaged over the residues of a region. Regions were the pocket lining defined above; the primer grip (residues 225–235); the YMDD motif (residues 183–186); and the p66 fingers (1–85, 118–155), thumb (237–318) and connection (319–426) subdomains. Side-chain χ1 for Tyr181 and Tyr188 was calculated as the N–Cα–Cβ–Cγ dihedral angle. Secondary structure was assigned per residue per frame by DSSP and reported as the fraction of a region's residues in helix or in strand. Observables corresponding to holo trajectories are reported by how each genotype differs from WT in one state. Observables corresponding to both holo and apo configurations report on the induced fit: how much binding DOR changes the observable, (bound − unliganded), and how far that change differs from WT. An induced fit near zero means the mutation shifts the bound and unliganded enzyme by the same amount.

red_paragraphs.paragraph: For experimental structure comparisons, sixteen NNIBP-lining Cα atoms were superposed betw
red_paragraphs.red_text: For experimental structure comparisons, sixteen NNIBP-lining Cα atoms were superposed between the DOR-bound structures (Protein Data Bank [PDB] IDs: 4NCG and 7Z2G44) and the RPV- (PDB ID: 2ZD1), EFV- (PDB ID: 1FK945) and NVP-bound (PDB ID: 1VRT46) structures. DOR heavy-atom RMSD, centroid displacement and internal conformation were compared between the two DOR structures; residue–DOR distances, pocket volumes and the Tyr181 and Tyr188 side-chain conformations were compared using the same structural definitions.

red_paragraphs.paragraph: To test whether the sampled DOR-bound state is recovered starting from gradually extreme p
red_paragraphs.red_text: To test whether the sampled DOR-bound state is recovered starting from gradually extreme perturbations to the starting configuration, alternative DOR poses were generated by random rigid-body placement within the NNIBP, screened to keep every ligand–protein heavy-atom contact above 2.2 Å, and accepted in 0.5 Å wide bands of heavy-atom RMSD from the crystallographic pose. Sixteen poses spanning 1.3 to 6.8 Å were prepared, minimized and simulated exactly as the production systems, one replicate each, but for 2 ns and without the 0.1 Å coordinate jitter used to decorrelate the production replicates. Endpoint pose coordinates are reported after superposition on the NNIBP Cα atoms as the DOR heavy-atom RMSD from the crystallographic pose, the displacement of the DOR centroid and the tilt of its long axis. Results are reported in Supplementary Section 3 and Supplementary Figure 2.

red_paragraphs.paragraph: For a series of N successive frames of a structural observable, with values xt and mean x̄
red_paragraphs.red_text: For a series of N successive frames of a structural observable, with values xt and mean x̄, sampled at interval Δt, the normalized autocorrelation function (ACF) was computed as , so that C(0) = 1; lags are reported as τΔt in nanoseconds. For block averaging, each series was partitioned into M = ⌊N/n⌋ non-overlapping blocks of length n with block means  where . The standard error of the mean implied by that block length, also called the blocked standard error, is . It rises with n and levels off once a block is longer than the correlation time of the observable, and that plateau is the standard error of the mean with correlation between frames accounted for. Block means were pooled across the three replicates of a genotype, so that even a 50 ns block yields six blocks from three 100 ns trajectories. Since g is the square of a ratio of estimated standard deviations, the interval shown on it is the chi-square interval on M − 1 degrees of freedom. The diagnostics are shown in Supplementary Section 4 and Supplementary Figure 3.

red_paragraphs.red_text: Minimizing each snapshot before the energy evaluation follows established practice for end-point methods. Minimization-based MM-PBSA has been validated for drug discovery,49 minimization-based MM-PBSA and MM-GBSA have been shown to reproduce the accuracy of ensemble averaging at a fraction of the cost,50 and minimizinga series of MD, as done here, has been shown to give results similar to single-point ensemble averages.34,51 Minimization relieves steric strain that single-point evaluation of frames sampled under explicit solvent, periodic boundary conditions and constrained bond lengths would otherwise carry intocutofffree, unconstrained implicit-solvent Hamiltonian used for scoring, where it contributes Lennard-Jones energies far larger than the binding signal. red_paragraphs.paragraph: Associations between the computed energies and phenotype were assessed by ordinary least-s
red_paragraphs.red_text: Agreement with phenotype was additionally summarized as a binary classification. A genotype was scored as predicted-resistant when the computed quantity (binding free energy or DOR-RT interaction energy), minus its standard error over replicates, exceeded +0.5 kcal/mol, approximately kBT at 300 K, and as predicted-susceptible otherwise. These classifications are referred to as strong and weak energetic effects, respectively. This cutoff was fixed a priori rather than fitted to the panel.

red_paragraphs.paragraph: Differences between genotypes in a structural observable were quantified with the replicat
red_paragraphs.red_text: Differences between genotypes in a structural observable were quantified with the replicate trajectory as the unit of comparison. For each genotype and observable we report the difference of replicate means — the effect size, in the observable's own units — its standard error, and a two-sided pooled-variance t-test on that difference, with the corresponding 95% confidence interval. A genotype-against-WT difference has 4 degrees of freedom and is resolved when it exceeds 2.78 standard errors; the induced fit, which is the interaction term of a genotype × ligand-state design, has 8 degrees of freedom and is resolved beyond 2.31. With three replicates per group, the variance estimate is itself imprecise, so these intervals are reported as descriptive bounds rather than as formal(Supplementary Table 4).

red_paragraphs.paragraph: To interrogate molecular mechanisms of DOR resistance, we started with the published X-ray
red_paragraphs.red_text: To interrogate molecular mechanisms of DOR resistance, we started with. This structure represents a minimal atomic scale 3D model of the local interactions within the NNIBP. It aligns well with an independent ternary structure of WT RT/DOR/DNA determined via cryo-EM,44 while demonstrating key differences, such as rotation of the Tyr181 sidechain, compared to experimentally determined structures of other NNRTI complexes with WT RT (Supplementary Text, Section 1). To further test robustness of the initial starting pose, we performed increasingly disruptive perturbations to the DOR pose within this structure and short 2ns equilibration simulations (Supplementary Text, Section 3). We find that perturbations up to 3 Å in DOR RMSD from the starting pose return to the sampled WT RT–DOR binding-pose basin (Supplementary Figure 2).

red_paragraphs.paragraph: In WT RT simulated here, binding DOR rotates Tyr181 by −18° and Tyr188 by +53°, from unlig
red_paragraphs.red_text: In WT RT simulated here, binding DOR rotates Tyr181 by −18° and Tyr188 by +53°, from unliganded values of −68° and −97° (Supplementary Table 4). A98G+F227C and G190S depart sharply from that pattern: their unliganded Tyr181 sits close to WT, at −68° and −52°, but binding drives it to −162° and −153°, a rotamer the WT complex does not adopt, giving induced-fit shifts of −76 ± 11° ([−101, −51]°, p < 0.001) and −83 ± 28° ([−148, −18]°, p = 0.02). The A98G+F227C value is the largest effect in Figure 5 relative to its error, at 6.9 standard errors. Y318F does the converse at Tyr188: its unliganded Tyr188 starts at +174°, a rotamer no other genotype visits, and DOR returns it to the common bound value of −38°, an induced-fit shift of +95 ± 32° ([22, 169]°, p = 0.02).

red_paragraphs.paragraph: Protein-level fluctuations and secondary structure are summarized in Supplementary Section
red_paragraphs.red_text: Protein-level fluctuations and secondary structure are summarized in Supplementary Section 8 and Supplementary Figure 5. In WT, binding DOR damps both regions we track: the pocket lining falls from 0.452 ± 0.011 Å unliganded to 0.361 ± 0.023 Å bound, and the primer grip from 0.570 ± 0.043 Å to 0.429 ± 0.021 Å (Supplementary Table 4). In A98G+F227C, the pocket lining is not damped at all, moving from 0.394 ± 0.027 Å to 0.415 ± 0.009 Å, an induced-fit shift of +0.11 ± 0.04 Å from WT ([0.02, 0.20] Å, p = 0.02) and the second largest effect in Figure 5. Its bound interface is otherwise close to WT, the only resolved contact metric being a −0.24 ± 0.06 Å change in the Val179 distance ([−0.40, −0.07] Å, p = 0.02).

red_paragraphs.paragraph: In K103N+M230L, the unliganded primer grip is markedly more mobile than WT, 0.772 ± 0.041
red_paragraphs.red_text: In K103N+M230L, the unliganded primer grip is markedly more mobile than WT, 0.772 ± 0.041 Å against 0.570 ± 0.043 Å, and binding DOR suppresses that excess, to 0.474 ± 0.012 Å (Supplementary Table 4). The induced fit is therefore twice that of WT, −0.30 Å against −0.14 Å, an induced-fit shift of −0.16 ± 0.06 Å ([−0.31, −0.01] Å, p = 0.04; Figure 5). K103N+M230L showed the largest DOR-associated reduction in primer-grip RMSF in the panel. V106I shows the same metric in the opposite direction, +0.14 ± 0.06 Å ([0.01, 0.27] Å, p = 0.04), its primer grip being equally mobile with and without the drug.

red_paragraphs.paragraph: The apo comparisons suggest that a mutation can alter the conformational response of RT to
red_paragraphs.red_text: The apo comparisons suggest that a mutation can alter the conformational response of RT to DOR binding even when contacts in the bound complex remain largely intact. In WT, DOR binding reduces fluctuations of the pocket-lining residues. In A98G+F227C, this reduction is smaller and is accompanied by a different binding-associated rotation of Tyr181, suggesting that DOR stabilizes a different local pocket arrangement. Y318F illustrates a complementary pattern: Tyr188 adopts a distinct rotamer in the unliganded enzyme but returns to a conformation close to WT in the DOR-bound complex. Examining the bound structures alone would therefore miss this difference in the starting conformational ensemble and the rearrangement associated with binding (Figure 5). These observations identify possible contributions from mutation-dependent changes in RT conformation and flexibility, although the simulations do not establish their energetic cost or whether they explain the observed resistance.

red_paragraphs.paragraph: There are three important limitations of this work. First, each system was simulated in tr
red_paragraphs.red_text: There are three important limitations of this work. First, each system was simulated in triplicate from a single seeded pose, so the replicates explore one basin of the bound ensemble and their agreement measures convergence within that basin. It is possible that there are several plausible RT-DOR conformations amongst the genotype panel that are not sampled here. Moreover, this limitation extends to the unliganded RT conformational ensembles, where the NNIBP without DOR may not equilibrate in 100ns. Of the 715 genotype-by-observable comparisons, 68 had 95% confidence intervals excluding zero, against approximately 36 expected at a nominal 5% threshold without correction for multiple comparisons (Supplementary Table 4). Most structural features in this panel are therefore unresolved at three replicates, and we distinguish the well-resolved local shifts from the more tentative conformational interpretations.

red_paragraphs.paragraph: Second, we simulate a binary RT–DOR complex with no template/primer and no incoming dNTP,
red_paragraphs.red_text: Second, we simulate a binary RT–DOR complex with no template/primer and no incoming dNTP, so a resistance mechanism acting through the nucleic-acid interface is structurally absent from our calculations. Specifically for this panel, Met230 and Pro225 both lie in the p66 primer grip, and a change in how the template is held, or in how often RT adopts a catalytically productive conformation, may not change ∆∆Gbind or ∆∆ETotal as we measure them, yet could still lower susceptibility in host cells. Agreement of the DOR pose and local pocket between the independent binary and DNA-bound experimental structures supports using this starting geometry for local drug-site comparisons (Supplementary Section 1, Supplementary Figure 1, and Supplementary Table 7). It does not establish that a simple RT-DOR model captures the conformational ensemble or catalytic coupling of substrate-bound RT.

red_paragraphs.paragraph: The third limitation is in the simulation forcefields. The two energy calculation methods
red_paragraphs.red_text: The third limitation is in the simulation forcefields. The two energy calculation methods in this study use different ligand charge models: the equilibrium simulations, and the MM/GBSA energies taken from them, use Gasteiger charges, whereas the alchemical legs use the AM1-BCC charges OpenFF assigns by default. This charge sensitivity can materially impact ∆∆ETotal ranking (Supplementary Table 5) because, even though the sign of an interface penalty is largely robust to the charge model; the rank of an individual genotype is not. Moreover, the shift falls almost entirely on the polar terms, and is largest where a substitution changes the formal charge. Note that MM/GBSA estimates are known to depend on the force field and the simulation protocol as much as on the structure being scored.34,51 We have therefore drawn conclusions where a sign or a rank order carries them, and have avoided resting an argument on a difference of about one kcal/mol. Nevertheless, this issue partly explains why several(Table 2).
